stock.counterargument: The honest counterargument is the sample: this process has not been shown to work, and a single ranking position is not evidence about one company.
invalidation: Quarterly revenue growth falling below +77.5%, the rate it was running at the quarter before.
Cash conversion dropping below 1.0×, meaning earnings stop being backed by cash.
A close below the 200-session average, which stood at $82.87 on the decision date.
risks: The share count is from 2026-06-30, 108 days older than the price, so the market capitalisation carries that staleness.
The most recent filing covers a period ending 2026-06-30, 108 days before the decision date.
One of the four quarters in the trailing year is the fourth quarter, which companies report only as part of the full year; it is derived as the annual figure less the first three quarters.
Point-in-time fundamentals are built from filings accepted up to 2026-10-16.

earnings.basis: the same fiscal quarter's announcement a year earlier (2025-11-06) plus 364 days

stock.rule: Universe: every US-listed common stock on NYSE, Nasdaq or NYSE American — about 4,700 names from Nasdaq Trader's own file. Eligible means: priced at $5 or more, median daily turnover of $20M or more over 60 sessions, at least 253 sessions of history, a 10-Q or 10-K whose period ended within 200 days, close above the 200-session average, volatility inside the day's 85th percentile, debt no more than 6× operating cash flow, no results announced in the last 2 sessions, and no position already open in the stock or a fourth in the same SIC division. Eligible candidates are then ranked on equally weighted z-scores within their sector group, over the signals that are defined for that group. One position per session, held 21 sessions, a twenty-first of capital each, 10 basis points of cost each way. Fundamentals are read as they stood on the decision date, never as they read today. The score is a ranking position among that day's eligible candidates. It is not a probability, a price target, or a forecast of any return.
stock.validation: The held-out window has not been opened. No claim of an edge is made or implied.

stories.title: Python's Mutable vs Immutable Types: What's the Difference?
stories.excerpt: Learn how Python mutable and immutable data types work internally and how you can use mutability or immutability to power your code.
stories.lead:
Python’s mutable objects, such as lists and dictionaries, allow you to change their value or data directly without affecting their identity. In contrast, immutable objects, like tuples and strings, don’t allow in-place modifications. Instead, you’ll need to create new objects of the same type with different values.

By the end of this tutorial, you’ll understand that:

In Python, mutability is a characteristic that may profoundly influence your decision when choosing which data type to use for solving a programming problem. Therefore, you need to know how mutable and immutable objects work in Python.

stories.title: How to Round Numbers in Python
stories.excerpt: Learn how Python's round() works, why it rounds 2.5 to 2, and how you can manage rounding errors with decimal, NumPy, and pandas.
stories.lead: Rounding numbers in Python is an essential task, especially when dealing with data precision. Python’s built-in round() function uses the rounding half to even strategy, which rounds numbers like 2.5 to 2 and 3.5 to 4. This method helps minimize rounding bias in datasets. To round numbers to specific decimal places, you can use the round() function with a second argument specifying the number of decimals.

stories.title: Django Migrations: A Primer
stories.excerpt: Get comfortable with Django migrations: create database tables without writing SQL, and keep your database in step as your models change.
stories.lead:
Since version 1.7, Django has come with built-in support for database migrations. In Django, database migrations usually go hand in hand with models: whenever you code up a new model, you also generate a migration to create the necessary table in the database. However, migrations can do much more.

In this article, you’ll get comfortable with Django migrations and learn the following:

If you are new to Django or web development in general, you might not be familiar with the concept of database migrations, and it might not seem obvious why they’re a good idea.

stories.lead:
In this quiz, you’ll test your understanding of Writing Comments in Python (Guide).

By working through this quiz, you’ll revisit how to write comments and docstrings in Python, when comments help you and your teammates, and which kinds of comments to avoid, like W.E.T., smelly, and rude ones.

The quiz contains 12 questions and there is no time limit. You’ll get 1 point for each correct answer. At the end of the quiz, you’ll receive a total score. The maximum score is 100%. Good luck!

stories.title: France's government under pressure after weekend of widespread violence
stories.excerpt: Political tension grips France after rioting marred protests over the cost of living and struggling public services, Katya Adler writes.
stories.lead:
France's Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu is holding a crisis cabinet meeting on Monday to assess a weekend of violence and looting across the country, in what were some of the worst scenes of public disorder in modern French history.

On Saturday over half a million mainly peaceful protesters demonstrated against rising living costs and dwindling access to decent public services, including a good state education. But the protests turned nasty after groups of black-clad, masked activists and vandals appeared.

stories.title: Trump endorses embattled Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu for reelection
stories.excerpt: Trump said in a post on social media that Netanyahu "has been a Great Warrior Prime Minister, and an even greater Partner for Peace in combatting the Islamic Republic of Iran."
stories.lead:
WEST PALM BEACH, Fla. — President Donald Trump on Sunday endorsed embattled Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu late in his reelection campaign, a coveted boost because of Trump's popularity but one that the American had withheld for months as the vote neared and the leaders' strategies in the Middle East diverged.

Israelis are set to vote Oct. 27, in the first national elections since Hamas attacked Israel on Oct. 7, 2023.

stories.title: Bollywood actor Tiger Shroff survives shooting attempt in Mumbai
stories.excerpt: Videos showed gunmen firing shots at Shroff's car while it was moving slowly past a crowd.
stories.lead:
Police in India's Mumbai city are investigating a shooting attempt on Bollywood actor Tiger Shroff, who survived without sustaining any gunshot wounds.

The 36-year-old was shot at on Sunday evening while he was in a car leaving a football ground in Juhu suburb. Videos showed at least two men firing multiple shots at close range at the front passenger seat of Shroff's car while it was moving slowly past a crowd.

Two people, including Shroff's driver, were injured, according to the police. Reports say three men have been detained in connection with the incident.

stories.title: Trump to close and renovate D.C. golf course, despite legal battle
stories.excerpt: President Trump continues his efforts to remake Washington, D.C. He wants to turn an area used by the public into a world-class golf course.
stories.lead:
President Trump has announced his plans to renovate the East Potomac Golf Links, a course in Washington D.C. that was already at the center of a testy legal battle.

In a Truth Social post on Sunday, Trump called the current course "old, broken, dilapidated, and of no further use or effect." According to the post, renovations will begin Nov. 15, and the course will be closed for approximately 15 months.

stories.title: What does a White House press secretary do?
stories.excerpt: Katie Zacharia's short time as White House press secretary has brought renewed attention to the high-profile role.
stories.lead:
The White House press secretary is one of the most important public-facing jobs in any administration. Yet it is one with no job description, no required qualifications, no vetting by Congress. And as the most recent press secretary found out, you can be fired from the position just as quickly as you were hired.

For nearly 100 years, since the rise of a modern press corp, there has been a person designated to speak on behalf of the sitting U.S. president. But the press secretary also answers to the public, says former Pentagon Press Secretary John Kirby. He served during both the Obama and Biden administrations.

stories.title: Anthropic says it will commit 5% of its shares to 'public benefit fund'
stories.excerpt: The announcement comes as Anthropic lays the ground for a blockbuster stock market listing.
stories.lead:
Artificial intelligence (AI) giant Anthropic says it will commit 5% of its shares to a fund that will make donations for the "public good".

The announcement comes as Anthropic lays the ground for a potential blockbuster stock market listing that could value the firm at more than $1tn (£750bn).

The AI industry has come under intense scrutiny recently over safety concerns and fears about its impact on society and the economy. Anthropic reportedly said in its initial public offering (IPO) filing that AI could pose "catastrophic or existential risks to humanity".

stories.excerpt: After Macron condemned ‘unbridled violence’, difference between French and German 10-year borrowing costs widens Business live – latest updates France was hit by a fresh wave of selling in its bond and stock markets on Monday after violent protests over the weekend left public buildings burned…
stories.lead:
France was hit by a fresh wave of selling in its bond and stock markets on Monday after violent protests over the weekend left public buildings burned, hundreds of shops looted and thousands of arrests across the country.

Almost 2,400 people have been arrested in France, the interior ministry said on Sunday, with police deploying teargas in confrontations with protesters.

The French president, Emmanuel Macron, condemned the “unbridled violence” in a televised address on Sunday night.

stories.title: People playing loud music on buses could face £100 fine
stories.excerpt: Antisocial behaviour on buses in England could lead to fines while a new campaign is also being launched for trains. A national campaign asking rail passengers "share the carriage, not the noise" is being launched.
stories.lead:
Passengers who play loud music on buses in England could be fined up to £100 under an attempt by the government to crack down on antisocial behaviour.

The measures also seek to tackle littering, vaping and threatening behaviour to help improve journeys on all forms of public transport.

Offenders on buses could be issued with the fines under new powers for local authorities.

stories.lead:
Ferencvaros won the Black Sea Cup 2026 after beating Pro Recco 15:18 in the final on Sunday. Balazs Nyeki’s side won all four of their games, and Akos Nagy led the way in the final with 5 goals from 6 shots.

Waspo Hannover took the bronze medal after coming back from two goals down late in the fourth quarter against Novi Beograd and winning the penalty shootout 4:2.
